title: A load check for orders
prompt: After every load, the data team logs a one-row summary of what arrived. Write `solve(orders)` so it returns how many rows and columns `orders` has, and the type its `total` column arrived as.
rules: One row with three columns, in order: `row_count`, `column_count` and `total_type`.
`row_count` and `column_count` are whole numbers of type `bigint`. Count every row, duplicates included.
`total_type` is the type exactly as `dtypes` writes it, for example `string` or `decimal(10,2)`.
hints: `orders.count()` counts the rows and `len(orders.columns)` counts the columns.
`dict(orders.dtypes)` lets you look up a column's type by its name.
Put the three values in one tuple and build the result with `spark.createDataFrame`. `BIGINT` in the schema gives `bigint`.
